lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: area of combined rectilinear figures

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

items.prompt: A rectangular garden bed is 6 ft long and 3 ft wide. What is its area?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: A rectangle 5 units long is split into two parts: one 2 units wide and one 4 units wide. Use 5 × (2 + 4) to find the total area.
A rectangular rug is 10 in long and 3 in wide. What is its area?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A rectangle 7 units long is split into two parts: one 4 units wide and one 4 units wide. Use 7 × (4 + 4) to find the total area.
A rectangular rug is 5 ft long and 8 ft wide. What is its area?
A rectangle 3 units long is split into two parts: one 3 units wide and one 6 units wide. Use 3 × (3 + 6) to find the total area.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A rectangular rug is 11 m long and 5 m wide. What is its area?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangle 3 units long is split into two parts: one 8 units wide and one 4 units wide. Use 3 × (8 + 4) to find the total area.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
